2nd Visit to Gogi house
Dec 2019
We originally visited this location back on our 2015 trip. We had a memorable experience there, so we obviously wanted to go back on this visit. 

We dined there on December 17th 2019. 

Unfortunately, this visit was not as memorable as our 2015 visit. As soon as we arrived, we felt that the vibe was off.

We ordered a premium sampler plate. All of the proteins we received were about 80% fat. 

Look, I realize this is a Korean bbq joint, and there is going to be fat on the meat (that's part of the great taste). In this case however, there was just so much fat and little meat, and whatever meat there was, was grisly. The protein was simply not enjoyable. 

When we came in 2015, the meat/protein was much better quality. We also were introduced to a sesame oil dipping sauce that had rock salt in it. 

When we asked for this dipping sauce during this visit, they looked oddly at us and brought out a giant bowl of sesame oil and giant bowl of salt. 

We explained to them in Vietnamese what we were looking for - and again - they had no idea. O'h well.....maybe the restaurant sold or changed management and they no longer have this dipping sauce. It's a shame cause it was awesome. 

Given the poor experience with the Premium Sampler plate, we order another protein (pork). the pork came but it was nearly frozen. Upon thawing through the cooking process, it utlimately cooked. 

The taste wasn't as good as our last visit in 2015. Again, I think the overall quality has gone downhill. Or, maybe we got them on an off night - who knows. 

We probably won't return to this Gogi. We'll either try another location or another restaurant entirely. 

Given our experience above, use caution, as your experience may vary.

Big Mistake
Apr 2018 • Couples
My friends and I visited this restaurant on Friday night. Keep in mind this is a Korean restaurant opened by Koreans from Korea. This is not a Vietnamese restaurant run by the locals because you would truly have a much better experience. This is just International money coming in to try and make more money with no regard for who their customers are and what their customers expectations are.

Here are the Pros and Cons

Pros:

1. Clean environment. Keep in mind that it is brand new restaurant. I also didn't visit the washrooms so not sure about those conditions.

2. Getting a table was very easy. I think because it is new and because the price is well above average, most people choose not to go there.

Cons:

1. It's hard to find an area to sit where you're not directly below in air conditioner. Trust me it gets really really cold and it'll ruin your whole experience since you're trying to barbecue using heat but yet you have cold air blasting down on your food.

2. The prices for the cheaper cuts of beef are not bad but not great. Therefore if you're looking for a more premium cut you have to spend three times as much. That would work out to about $15 Canadian for one order of Premium cut and that's not even the top of the line. For the people that state that it is cheap that's because they're purchasing the Lesser Quality Meat

3. They charge for wet naps. Yes that is correct so regardless of if you bring your own napkins you're still getting charged automatically for wet naps. And they automatically charge you per person that sitting at the table.

4. The bill is in Vietnamese and therefore it's hard to ascertain what you are charged for and unless you are in a small group like you and maybe your significant other it's easier to tell but in a bigger group I can assure you they're sneaking in a lot more things. 

5. Staff doesn't smile...at all! They will however fill your request but sometimes it will take a while.

6. They want you to order your dessert at the same time that you're placing your initial order. They will then decide when to bring you your dessert. And I can assure you while you're still trying to cook your meal you'll have dessert sitting right there on the table melting away especially if you ordered anything off their dessert menu which majority of it is frozen like ice cream. I had to actually have someone else eat my dessert because I was still trying to eat my main meal. This is probably the most ridiculous thing I have ever experienced in any restaurant in any part of the world in my entire life.

Important note: When the bill came and we handed over the cash or I should say Vietnamese Dong but regardless of what currency they never returned to give us the change. Yes that's right they actually kept the change. We're not in Canada or the US so to leave a $5 tip off of a $20 purchase in a country with a $5 can buy you two meals at a mom-and-pop type shop is absolutely asinine.

The whole point of being in a country like Vietnam is your dollar goes a long long way. Therefore for them to automatically assume that you're leaving a $5 tip and more than happy to pay for their wet naps is absolutely ridiculous. Hence, I advise you based on the quality of food the price of the food the not so smiley service I wouldn't even spend $0.50 in this place.

My advice to you is when there's so many other restaurants that have been in business longer, definitely stick with them you won't be disappointed

It's not worth it to go try a new restaurant in a city like this where the experiences are extremely affordable and in this case literally cost you a lot more and there's a greater chance of you being let down.
